subject: POC plan & risk tracker - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@acme.com>, Michael Ortiz <m.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC plan & risk tracker - Acme Corp

Hi Sophie / Michael,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the POC plan we discussed so we can lock timelines and owners. Please review and confirm by EOD Tuesday so we can schedule the kickoff.

POC overview (2-week evaluation):
- Goal: Validate real-world latency, cost, and quality for your customer-facing summarization use case (50-200 tokens per request).
- Scope: 10k sample conversations, integration via S3 connector, Redwood hosted inference with option to test Dedicated node.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Average 95th-percentile latency <= 300ms on test workload.
2) Summaries meet baseline NIST-like ROUGE / human score (>= 0.78 on our eval set).
3) No data leakage and SOC2-aligned controls for PII-handling during the POC.
4) Cost per 1k requests under your target threshold (TBD by you).

Evaluation plan & owners:
- Data ingestion & test set: Acme (Michael)
- Integration & infra: Redwood eng (Vivek, Dev)
- Success validation / human eval: Acme PM (Sophie) + Redwood Solutions (Marissa)

High-level timeline:
- Confirm plan: by 2026-06-01
- Kickoff & infra prep: 2026-06-08
- POC window: 2026-06-09 through 2026-06-23 (2 weeks)
- Final review: week of 2026-06-29

Risk and issue tracking (initial):
- Blocking connector issues or model-inference failures: escalate to Vivek (technical lead) immediately.
- Data access / security questions: Jamal (security contact) included once you confirm.
- We will maintain a shared tracker and a daily 15-min standup during the POC.

Attachments: POC-MAP.xlsx (POC milestones), POC-RISKS.xlsx (initial risks).

Ask: Please confirm the success criteria and add your security contact to the thread. If that looks good, I will send calendar invites and a kickoff agenda.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect as a starting point. A couple of quick notes:
- SOC2 / security: I9ll add Jamal Harris (Security) to confirm controls and the questionnaire.
- Success criteria: Can we split the cost target into two tiers (hosted vs dedicated)? I9ll send target numbers separately.
- Data subset: we will provide a redacted sample of 2k conversations for the first week, then full 10k if all goes well.

I9ll loop Jamal into this thread after I9ve confirmed with him.

Appreciate the notes, Sophie. Confirming next steps based on your feedback:
- We9ll add Jamal to the thread once you give the go-ahead.
- We9ll publish two cost-tier estimates (hosted vs dedicated) by 2026-06-01.
- We will include a pause-and-incident workflow: if model-quality drops below your agreed threshold, we will pause ingestion and escalate.

Mitigations for common risks:
- Blocking connector bug: fallback to batch S3 ingestion for the first 24 hours while engineering works on live connector fix.
- Model regression: freeze rollout and open an incident with engineering and product owners (Redwood: Vivek / Dev; Acme: Sophie / Michael).
- Data security question: we attach SOC2-questionnaire.pdf for Jamal to review.

I9ve attached the SOC2 questionnaire and updated the POC-MAP to reflect the pause workflow. Once you confirm, I9ll schedule the kickoff for 2026-06-08 and set up the daily standups (15 minutes).

Attachments: SOC2-questionnaire.pdf, updated POC-MAP.xlsx.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-02T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC plan & risk tracker - Acme Corp

Quick technical note on risks and escalation:

Potential blocking issue we discussed: On-prem S3 connector + quantized model path can hit a memory pinning bug for sequence lengths > 512, causing OOMs on certain GPU types. Likelihood: moderate for your longest conversations. Impact: POC could stall if we hit it early.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
- Start with the redacted 2k sample (as planned) and cap sequence length to 512 for the first 48 hours.
- If OOMs occur, switch to the CPU fallback for ingestion and continue validation on a smaller sample while we debug.
- Assign debug owners: Vivek (Redwood eng lead), Dev (hotfix owner). If we cannot resolve within 48 hours, escalate to Lukas Meyer (VP Eng) for capacity/temp node allocation.

Operational items:
- Create a dedicated Slack channel #poc-acme-rdw-4571 for real-time alerts.
- Daily 10:00am standup during POC (15 mins).
- Tracker ownership: Marissa will maintain the risk tracker; Vivek will update technical status.

I9ll draft a short runbook for the OOM debugging steps and post it to the Drive link.

-Vivek
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@acme.com>

Date: 2026-06-05T16:48:00-07:00

Thanks Vivek — I can own the hotfix path. If we hit the memory pinning OOM we will:
1) Collect logs and core dumps to S3 (automated script I9ll provide).
2) Patch runtime within a dev hotfix branch; target turnaround 24-36 hours.
3) If patch exceeds 36 hours, request temporary Dedicated node allocation from Lukas for a brute-force test/resolution.

I9ll prepare the ingestion fallback script and upload it to the shared Drive. Also recommend we reserve 1 Dedicated slot for the first 48 hours of the POC as a safety net. Can Marissa confirm allocation so I can queue resources?

-Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
